nodes.label: Customer-Variable Page Count
nodes.description: First product type where surface count is customer state. Template declares pageCount: {min, max, step, default}; customer types a count, inner pages auto-populate from the single inner-page template. Steps in multiples of 4 (signature folding).

nodes.label: Gutter / Spine Margin
nodes.description: book.gutterMm — inner margin auto-mirrored by page parity (odd pages bind left, even bind right). Shift is half the gutter figure applied uniformly across a page's frames/overlays, capped by tightest element's headroom.

nodes.label: Spine Width Formula
nodes.description: spineWidthMm = (pageCount/2 leaves) × paperThicknessMm — computed dimension recomputed whenever customer changes page count. Implementation differs from PRD sketch (which double-counted) — needs Catalog Ops sign-off.

nodes.label: pagesToSpreads
nodes.description: services/book_layout.py::pages_to_spreads() and lib/book-layout.ts::pagesToSpreads() — groups flat page list into spread pairs for read-only preview. Page 1 alone, then facing pairs, last alone, covers always alone.

nodes.label: DPDP Erasure Gap (CLOSED)
nodes.description: PRD documenting closed erasure bug: purge reported success while photos remained on disk. Root cause: autosave blanked CanvasData.image_paths every 2s. Fixed in migration 0011 with UploadedFile.order_id linkage and directory-based purge.

nodes.label: UploadedFile.order_id
nodes.description: order_id field added to UploadedFile in migration 0011. Populated from X-Order-ID header at upload. Makes erasure provable without depending on canvas state. Direct partner API uploads record blank order_id.

nodes.label: Order-Scoped Upload Paths
nodes.description: Uploads stored under UPLOADS_DIR/<order_id>/ — ownership visible in path. Purge deletes the directory outright, finding files even without a DB row. Dot-leading and dot-only order_ids rejected to prevent path traversal.

nodes.label: Book Layout Parity Tests
nodes.description: TS↔Python parity test suites: frontend/nextjs/src/lib/__tests__/book-layout.parity.test.ts and backend/django/services/tests/test_book_layout_parity.py. Pins geometry math (gutter mirroring, spread grouping) against a shared fixture.

nodes.label: Phase 2: S3Storage + get_storage factory
nodes.rationale: S3Storage fail-fast on missing AWS creds; list_layouts queries LayoutCatalogue (no S3 LIST); multipart assemble_chunks with cleanup on failure; key prefixes uploads/{order_id}/, masks/, exports/, ops-config/.

nodes.label: Phase 3: views query LayoutCatalogue
nodes.rationale: ListLayoutsView, GetLayoutView, EditorInitView, LayoutManagementView, ExternalLayoutDetailView switched from filesystem to ORM; cache keys/TTL/response schema unchanged; EditorInitView reuses GetLayoutView cache keys.

nodes.label: Atomic layout cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: invalidate_layout_caches deletes layouts_list_all + ops_layouts_list_all + layout_detail:{name}:* together, wrapped so it never fails the API; on rename clears both names. Prevents silent wrong-print bugs from a stale cached layout.

nodes.label: Phase 4: MaskDownloadView presigned URLs + mask upload
nodes.rationale: S3: presigned URL (1 h) + 301; local: FileResponse; path traversal guard; mask embedded as layout['maskUrl'].

nodes.label: Mask key migration on layout rename
nodes.rationale: copy_object then delete_file; non-fatal on failure (logs warning, still HTTP 200); tries common extensions until the mask is found.

nodes.label: Phase 5: services/asset_store.py S3-first with local fallback
nodes.rationale: read_asset(asset_type, asset_name) for calendar_styles/holidays/palettes/fonts; tries S3 ops-config/ then local; AssetNotFoundError only when both fail; readers keep a 5-min Redis cache.

nodes.rationale: api/tests/test_layout_catalogue.py and test_cache_invalidation.py; runbook with 7 success criteria and ~1 h timeline.

nodes.rationale: EditorRenderView queries LayoutCatalogue by name, snapshots definition, dispatches render_canvas_task; engine loads layout from DB snapshot not disk.

nodes.rationale: S3 untested in prod (run STORAGE_BACKEND=local); calendar asset writes still go to disk; GenerateLayoutView still read layouts from disk at time of writing (CLAUDE.md later records this as fixed in the 2026-09-04 audit).

nodes.label: Phased rollout rationale
nodes.rationale: Model first (no risk until migration runs), backends in parallel (no immediate switching), views one type at a time, mask/asset support on top (disableable), comprehensive tests before prod.

nodes.label: Design: LayoutCatalogue field table
nodes.rationale: name CharField(255) unique case-sensitive overrides definition['name']; product_type inferred from definition.productType default single_canvas; version bumped per write; imported_at/imported_by co-validated in clean(). Composite indexes (product_type,is_deprecated) and (is_deprecated,is_public).

nodes.label: Design: S3Storage backend
nodes.rationale: Layouts from Postgres, masks/uploads/exports/ops-config in S3; __init__ raises ImproperlyConfigured naming missing env vars; boto3 client.

nodes.label: Design: services/asset_store.py read_asset
nodes.rationale: _VALID_ASSET_TYPES frozenset; ValueError on unknown type; delegates to get_storage().read_calendar_asset; callers CalendarStylesView, HolidaysView, _read_fonts.

nodes.label: Property 1: cache invalidation completeness
nodes.rationale: Invalidation always attempted after a write even if the write raised; list caches deleted even when the detail pattern delete fails. Validates Req 7.1, 7.5, 7.6.

nodes.label: Property 2: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: select_for_update on the old row inside transaction.atomic so no request observes old and new both non-deprecated. Validates Req 6.7, 6.8.

nodes.label: Property 3: migration idempotency
nodes.rationale: update_or_create(name=...) so applying 0016 twice leaves the same row set. Validates Req 2.2, 11.1.

nodes.label: Property 5: mask copy-before-delete
nodes.rationale: Never delete a mask key before a successful copy; copy failure → 500 with original untouched; delete failure after copy → orphan logged, 200.

nodes.label: Design: cache key reference (unchanged)
nodes.rationale: layouts_list_all (ListLayoutsView), ops_layouts_list_all (LayoutManagementView.get), layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces} (GetLayoutView, EditorInitView); all 120 s; all invalidated by invalidate_layout_caches.

nodes.label: Design Phase 6: .gitignore storage dirs
nodes.rationale: Ignore storage/layouts, masks, calendar_styles, calendar_palettes, holidays to break the git-conflict cycle; prod_layouts.json IS committed as the data handoff artifact.

nodes.label: Req 1: LayoutCatalogue data model
nodes.rationale: Fields, case-sensitive byte-for-byte unique name, indexes, auto timestamps, imported_at/imported_by co-validation.

nodes.label: Req 2: Migration 0016 schema + idempotent import
nodes.rationale: update_or_create per entry; malformed entries logged and skipped; NOP reverse; missing prod_layouts.json → warn and succeed; non-array root → error and skip.

nodes.label: Req 3: S3Storage backend
nodes.rationale: Fail-fast ImproperlyConfigured on missing AWS vars; implements every StorageBackend method; list_layouts never LISTs S3; multipart assemble with abort on failure.

nodes.label: Req 4: ListLayoutsView serves from DB
nodes.rationale: Merge definition + name + hasCalendar; layouts_list_all cached 120 s; ?fields=summary; always {layouts: [...]}; DB error → 500 with detail.

nodes.label: Req 5: GetLayoutView serves from DB
nodes.rationale: Path guard first (400 before any query); 404 on miss; layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces} cached 120 s; surfaces filter case-insensitive, empty array not 404.

nodes.label: Req 6: LayoutManagementView writes to DB
nodes.rationale: update_or_create returns 200/201; soft-delete sets is_deprecated; rename atomic in one transaction with 409 on conflict; invalidate caches after every write.

nodes.label: Req 7: atomic cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: Bulk-delete both list keys together; delete layout_detail:{name}:* pattern; AttributeError → fallback to unparameterised key; other exceptions logged, never propagated.

nodes.label: Req 8: mask serving via presigned URLs
nodes.rationale: S3: 301 to presigned URL with 300–3600 s expiry; local: 200 with file; guard first; 404 on missing; 502 on other S3 errors without detail.
nodes.norm_label: req 8: mask serving via presigned urls

nodes.label: Req 9: mask upload to S3 and rename copy-before-delete
nodes.norm_label: req 9: mask upload to s3 and rename copy-before-delete

nodes.label: Req 10: calendar assets under ops-config/ with local fallback
nodes.norm_label: req 10: calendar assets under ops-config/ with local fallback

nodes.label: Req 11: deployment and rollback
nodes.rationale: Migration applies automatically on container start; STORAGE_BACKEND=local claimed to restore filesystem behaviour without DB rollback (not implemented per runbook); reverse is NOP.

nodes.label: Req 12: API contract preservation
nodes.rationale: Identical response shapes and status codes; masks endpoint stays on the embed allowlist without a privilege gate.

nodes.label: Path_Traversal_Guard (_is_safe_layout_name)
nodes.rationale: Rejects names containing /, \, .., or a leading .; always the first validation step before any DB or S3 call.

nodes.label: Soft_Delete via is_deprecated
nodes.rationale: Preserves audit trail while hiding from public reads.

nodes.label: Runbook: export prod layout catalogue before 0016
nodes.rationale: Run export_layout_catalogue.py against storage/layouts on prod, verify count matches filesystem, scp and commit backend/migrations/prod_layouts.json.
nodes.norm_label: runbook: export prod layout catalogue before 0016

nodes.label: Pillow==10.3.0
nodes.rationale: pillow-heif is pinned to the release that resolves against Pillow 10.3.0 — do NOT bump Pillow to chase a newer pillow-heif without re-testing the render pipeline.

nodes.label: pillow-heif==0.22.0
nodes.rationale: Bundles libheif 1.19 as a manylinux wheel. Exists because browser-side heic2any (2021 libheif) cannot read iOS 18 tmap gain-map HEIC and Chrome/Firefox have no HEIC codec; used by services/heic.py behind POST /api/heic/convert.

nodes.label: mediapipe==0.10.18
nodes.rationale: Loaded lazily by services/orientation.py for POST /api/orientation/detect; ~200 MB docker layer (tflite-runtime, opencv-headless, numpy, protobuf); workers install it but never import it.

nodes.label: Inter-Variable.ttf
nodes.rationale: One well-engineered variable font (weights 100-900 in a single 859 KB file, Apache 2.0 / SIL OFL) serves every weight; bundled in the Docker image under services/fonts_assets/.

nodes.label: Single bundled font, no font picker (PRD §11.7)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding one font eliminates a class of production failure modes (font missing, preview/print drift) and removes the need for a picker for ops or customers.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled font, no font picker (prd §11.7)

nodes.label: Fallback to PIL default bitmap font
nodes.rationale: If the .ttf is absent the renderer still ships output, just with ugly text, and logs a warning — degrade rather than fail the render.
nodes.norm_label: fallback to pil default bitmap font

nodes.label: Boot-time startup_check() for missing font
nodes.rationale: Flags a missing font in the Django log at boot so deploys never silently degrade.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: OFL §1-3 explicitly permit bundling the .ttf in the Docker image and shipping it inside rendered PNGs.

nodes.label: Contract if a font picker is ever added
nodes.rationale: Would reverse §11.7: read names from storage/fonts.json, resolve each to <FamilyName>.ttf in fonts_assets/, and add a startup check that every JSON entry has a matching .ttf. Until then any extra .ttf is dead weight.
nodes.norm_label: contract if a font picker is ever added

nodes.label: STORAGE_ROOT env var
nodes.rationale: Single env-driven root (default ./storage) from which LAYOUTS_DIR, EXPORTS_DIR and UPLOADS_DIR derive, so redirecting one variable redirects every path.

nodes.label: storage/fonts.json (FONTS_JSON_PATH)
nodes.rationale: Font .ttf files ship with the image under services/fonts_assets/, not under STORAGE_ROOT — correct because fonts are immutable assets.

nodes.label: Local-filesystem atomic writes — the single S3 blocker
nodes.rationale: Three callers do tempfile + os.replace atomic writes. S3 PutObject is already atomic per object, so each becomes write-temp → upload → delete, or boto3.upload_fileobj.
nodes.norm_label: local-filesystem atomic writes — the single s3 blocker

nodes.label: LayoutEngine._write_output_atomic
nodes.rationale: Stages the temp file in the same directory as the final output so it stays within STORAGE_ROOT.

nodes.label: RenderJobDownloadView ZIP built under EXPORTS_DIR
nodes.rationale: The temp ZIP lives under EXPORTS_DIR so it inherits whatever backing store STORAGE_ROOT points at.

nodes.label: services/blob_store.py shim (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Wrap reads (open → boto3.get_object) and writes behind one shim so the three callers stay unchanged during the S3 move.

nodes.label: Per-day entries as one flat { iso_date: [CellOverride] } map
nodes.rationale: Shipped instead of the 12-slot cellsPerCanvas array: entries anchor to globally-unique ISO dates so photo-canvas count changes and English↔Financial flips can never lose or misplace them. Legacy 12-slot arrays are still read on restore.
nodes.norm_label: per-day entries as one flat { iso_date: [celloverride] } map

nodes.label: Photo → month mapping capped at 12 (month i uses photo canvas i mod N)
nodes.rationale: 1 photo cycles to all 12 months, 12 map one-per-month; upload order matters. An earlier build emitted 12·N files in the ZIP.
nodes.norm_label: photo → month mapping capped at 12 (month i uses photo canvas i mod n)

nodes.label: Calendar primitive — a layout-agnostic positioned region
nodes.rationale: Defined by {x,y,width,height} percentages; owns only the grid, cells, pills, holidays and per-cell editing so desk, full-page, poster and side-by-side products come free via layout authoring.
nodes.norm_label: calendar primitive — a layout-agnostic positioned region

nodes.label: Server renderer drew no overlays (pre-v1.12 gap)
nodes.rationale: engine.py had zero ImageDraw/ImageFont imports; text/shape/image overlays were preview-only and vanished from the print. A hard prerequisite for the calendar and valuable on its own.
nodes.norm_label: server renderer drew no overlays (pre-v1.12 gap)

nodes.label: Design principle — minimal customer-facing controls ('templates, not configurators')
nodes.rationale: Every knob is a chance to produce output the design team would not ship; fewer controls cost less to maintain, produce fewer support tickets and protect print quality. Customers wanting more pick a different layout.
nodes.norm_label: design principle — minimal customer-facing controls ('templates, not configurators')

nodes.label: Layout-authored, customer-overridden two-layer model
nodes.rationale: Template (position/size/style) in layout JSON owned by ops; overrides (year, month, cells) in CanvasData.editor_state owned by the customer.

nodes.label: CalendarCellOverride (text | image | hide)
nodes.rationale: Text entries are text-only; dot colour rotates through a 3-slot per-theme cycle by entry index so multi-entry cells stay distinguishable without a picker.

nodes.label: Cells keyed by ISO date, no cell IDs
nodes.rationale: Month change re-derives the cell set automatically; overrides for dates not in the new month stay in the JSON in case the customer flips back.
nodes.norm_label: cells keyed by iso date, no cell ids

nodes.label: Month-grid algorithm (identical client + server math)
nodes.rationale: firstCellOffset = (firstDay - weekStart + 7) % 7; totalCells = ceil((offset + daysInMonth)/7) × 7 → 28/35/42; cellW = usableWidth/7.

nodes.label: Z-order tower — calendar above overlays, below mask
nodes.rationale: calendarZ = overlayZStart + overlays.length + 1 so the calendar is always on top of artwork and the layout mask still wins.
nodes.norm_label: z-order tower — calendar above overlays, below mask

nodes.label: date-fns for month-grid date math
nodes.rationale: ~6 KB tree-shaken; saves ~30 LOC and gives Intl-aware weekday names.

nodes.label: Auto-fit text via ImageFont.getbbox() binary search
nodes.rationale: No library fits either side: DOM auto-fit libs cannot see a <canvas>, and Pillow has no auto-fit — the documented community pattern is ~15 LOC.
nodes.norm_label: auto-fit text via imagefont.getbbox() binary search

nodes.label: Cell images reuse smartcrop + cover-fit + auto-orientation
nodes.rationale: Each cell is a tiny frameSpec, so calculateSmartCropOffsets and _composite_canvas cover math plus the v1.11 MediaPipe pipeline apply with zero new logic.
nodes.norm_label: cell images reuse smartcrop + cover-fit + auto-orientation

nodes.label: Reuse-vs-build cheat-sheet
nodes.rationale: Pure reuse: chunked upload, UploadedFile + GC, IDB persistence, auto-orientation, smartcrop, debouncedRender, fonts endpoint, editor_state, LayoutManagementView, z-order tower, cache invalidation, embed token resolution.

nodes.label: services/overlay_renderer.py — render_overlays()
nodes.rationale: Draws text/shape/image overlays via Pillow ImageDraw after frame compositing and before the paper mask.

nodes.label: services/calendar_renderer.py — render_calendar()
nodes.rationale: Called after render_overlays so the calendar is always on top, matching client z-order.

nodes.label: CalendarEditPanel.tsx — per-cell customer editor
nodes.rationale: Bottom-sheet on narrow viewports because 42 tiny tap targets on a phone is painful.

nodes.label: api/validators.py calendar-block validation
nodes.rationale: Range checks on positions, monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12, banned fields in surfaceOverrides.

nodes.label: TS↔Python grid parity tests (shared fixtures)
nodes.rationale: Any drift between lib/calendar.ts and services/calendar_renderer.py fails CI; both sides consume the same ground truth.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Server-side overlay rendering (v1.12, ~4 d)
nodes.rationale: The unblocker for everything; ships on its own.

nodes.label: Risk — Pillow text rendering quality vs browser hinting
nodes.rationale: Mitigation: side-by-side diff in Phase 1; stick to Inter as the safe default.
nodes.norm_label: risk — pillow text rendering quality vs browser hinting

nodes.label: Risk — i18n scope creep
nodes.rationale: Lock v1 to weekStart monday|sunday, Intl weekday names, holidays for en-IN and generic only.

nodes.label: Pill-style cell entries (date always visible, entries stack below)
nodes.norm_label: pill-style cell entries (date always visible, entries stack below)

nodes.label: 3-slot dotCycle per theme / palette
nodes.rationale: Pill background is one theme-wide colour; the dot rotates by entry index so 1st/2nd/3rd entries are distinct without exposing a colour picker.

nodes.label: Global holiday auto-load (holidaySource)
nodes.rationale: Frontend fetches holidays for (locale, year) and injects source:'holiday' entries; the customer cannot delete them but can override the cell with an image.

nodes.label: Three style presets (JSON in storage/calendar_styles/)
nodes.rationale: Ops picks one when authoring; the preset's style block is copied into the layout JSON and can be fine-tuned.

nodes.label: modern-genz preset (4 coordinated palettes)
nodes.rationale: Each palette sets all 6 colour roles together plus a dotCycle; the swatch is the only Gen-Z customer control. New palettes ship as JSON files with no code change.

nodes.label: weekday-highlight preset (Sunday stands out)
nodes.rationale: Single visual cue — light-red fill + red date; no border because it read as a state indicator in review.

nodes.label: Gen-Z palettes (Butter & Purple, Mint & Hot Pink, Lilac & Coral, Sky & Lemon)
nodes.norm_label: gen-z palettes (butter & purple, mint & hot pink, lilac & coral, sky & lemon)

nodes.label: Zero new DB migrations
nodes.rationale: All new data is JSON-shape in existing free-form columns (layout JSON, editor_state); old states deserialise cleanly with the field absent.

nodes.label: productType: 'calendar' — a Multi-Surface Product with a flag
nodes.rationale: Not a separate category (would fork render/ops/preview pipelines) and not pure multi-surface (ops would hand-build 12 surfaces and keep global controls in sync). The flag lets the system auto-generate 12 surfaces from one template with no changes to render, embed or webhook code.
nodes.norm_label: producttype: 'calendar' — a multi-surface product with a flag

nodes.label: Single-template authoring + 12-surface auto-generation
nodes.rationale: Ops designs ONE representative month; the system materializes 12 surfaces at mount / render.

nodes.label: Surface index → (year, month) resolution formula
nodes.rationale: totalOffset = surfaceIndex + (monthOffset ?? 0); realMonth = ((startMonth-1+totalOffset) % 12)+1; realYear = baseYear + floor((startMonth-1+totalOffset)/12).

nodes.label: surfaceOverrides — sparse per-month structural overrides
nodes.rationale: Field-level replace, not deep merge: merging arrays is ambiguous (by id? concatenate? positional?) and each interpretation leaks into UX. Untouched fields inherit from the template; only the diff is persisted.

nodes.label: Ops vs customer control split (§10.3)
nodes.rationale: Aspect ratio and week start ops-locked; theme preset, Gen-Z palette and calendar type customer-changeable; year auto-populated.

nodes.label: defaultYear: 'current' — auto-rolling year
nodes.rationale: Layout files never freeze to a year; a layout published in 2026 prints 2027 dates from Jan 1, 2027 with zero ops intervention.

nodes.label: Calendar type — English (Jan..Dec) vs Financial (Apr..Mar)
nodes.rationale: Same SKU; baseYear = today.month >= Apr ? year : year-1 for financial. Drives startMonth so it must stay layout-global.

nodes.label: Photobook as the next productType
nodes.rationale: Reuses multi-surface render, single-template authoring, embed/ZIP/webhook; differs in variable N, no calendar primitive, spreads.

nodes.label: productType is the extension point for new products
nodes.rationale: Each productType gets its own ops and preview UIs but shares the storage + render layer.
nodes.norm_label: producttype is the extension point for new products

nodes.label: Multi-calendar single-surface (year-on-one-poster) mode
nodes.rationale: monthRange.count = 1, calendars.length = 12, each with explicit monthOffset.

nodes.label: Constraint: monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12
nodes.rationale: Validator rejects other products; mixed grids are mathematically valid but the UI ships only the two patterns.

nodes.label: Cell-image expiry — 'Image expired, please re-upload'
nodes.rationale: Follows the UploadedFile GC policy; no automatic recovery because embed sessions are short-lived enough that this is rare.

nodes.label: Calendar type flip warning modal (orphaned entries hidden, not deleted)
nodes.norm_label: calendar type flip warning modal (orphaned entries hidden, not deleted)

nodes.label: Multi-surface partial failure — fail-all-or-nothing
nodes.rationale: If any 1 of N surfaces fails the whole RenderJob fails and retry re-renders all N; per-surface retry is v2.

nodes.label: ZIP filenames from displayLabel ('January 2026.png')
nodes.rationale: Financial-year calendars span 'April 2026.png … March 2027.png'; non-calendar multi-surface products use the ops-set label.

nodes.label: §11.7 — Single bundled font (Inter Variable), no picker
nodes.rationale: Removes fontFamily/fontWeight from the schema: no font drift between preview and 300 DPI render, simpler authoring, and the 'font missing' failure mode is eliminated.
nodes.norm_label: §11.7 — single bundled font (inter variable), no picker

nodes.label: Feb 29 entries on non-leap years — one-time toast, entries kept
nodes.norm_label: feb 29 entries on non-leap years — one-time toast, entries kept

nodes.label: scripts/refresh-holidays.py — annual ops task
nodes.rationale: A year without a holiday file renders with no auto-injection rather than an error.

nodes.label: Hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no '+N more'
nodes.norm_label: hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no '+n more'

nodes.label: MAX_ENTRIES precedence — user-first
nodes.rationale: Reverses the original holidays-first rule: customer intent beats auto-injection; a suppressed holiday reappears when a user entry is removed.

nodes.label: Out-of-month filler cells — date number only
nodes.rationale: No entries, pills or images: cleaner and avoids 'is this entry for this month or the next?' ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: out-of-month filler cells — date number only

nodes.label: IST-only, ISO date strings end-to-end
nodes.rationale: The renderer never calls datetime.now(); the frontend computes 'today' in Asia/Kolkata. All v1 customers are in India.

nodes.label: Validator rejects banned fields in surfaceOverrides
nodes.rationale: themePreset, calendarType, weekStart, canvas, monthRange are layout-global; banning them stops ops bypassing the rule via manual JSON edits.
nodes.norm_label: validator rejects banned fields in surfaceoverrides

nodes.label: No layout versioning — fresh load on every embed
nodes.rationale: Acceptable for v1 because sessions are short-lived and ops rarely edits published layouts mid-quarter; add layoutVersion if edit frequency rises.
nodes.norm_label: no layout versioning — fresh load on every embed

nodes.label: v2 readiness — signed S3 download URL
nodes.rationale: The Next.js proxy buffers full ZIPs (~300 MB peak); v1 keeps download_url, RenderJobDownloadView and the output path S3-friendly so v2 is a contained swap.
nodes.norm_label: v2 readiness — signed s3 download url

nodes.label: Reuse of storage/fonts.json + FontsView (original proposal)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by §11.7's single bundled font.

nodes.label: Why the pe-callback Webhook Exists
nodes.rationale: Product Editor is a standalone print-file generator that does not push files into Printo's OMS or any other backend, so completion must be communicated to the storefront via a signed webhook rather than a direct internal push; printo.in's handler then verifies the signature, fetches the ZIP, and attaches it to the order.

nodes.label: Why the ZIP Was Split Into Four URLs
nodes.rationale: download_url is unchanged/not deprecated so existing integrations need no change; the three split URLs (print/mock/uploads) were added Aug 2026 for storefronts that keep mock and print in separate fields, so they can fetch each directly instead of unpacking and sorting one combined archive. Nothing is duplicated on disk — the split is served by a ?content= filter over the same rendered files.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Over/Under-Quota Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Over-qty is blocked on both the editor and POST /api/editor/render; under-qty is only warned about and still allowed on both sides. qty is caller-supplied, so treating it as a hard gate in both directions would risk stranding a real order at checkout on a wrong value — the storefront should re-check file_count on the completion webhook if it needs a guaranteed count.

nodes.label: Why qty Moved Off the Iframe URL
nodes.rationale: The iframe URL never carries qty; it is stored on the session, injected as a header the browser never sees, and re-checked at submit directly against EmbedSession — so the customer cannot raise the cap by editing the URL, and the cap holds even for a direct POST to /api/editor/render that bypasses the iframe.

nodes.label: Layout Rename Alias Fallback (Sep 16, 2026)
nodes.rationale: Before Sep 16, 2026, an ops rename of a layout identifier 404'd the storefront's iframe permanently with no signal; the fix keeps the old identifier resolving indefinitely by aliasing it across /api/editor/init, /api/layouts/<name>, and the render pipeline, so no storefront-side action is required.

nodes.label: Why pe:back Doesn't Use Browser History
nodes.rationale: An iframe has no back/forward stack of its own — browsers keep one shared history per tab across the parent page and every frame in it — so calling browser-back from inside the iframe risks navigating the parent page unpredictably or carrying the customer off the storefront entirely mid-checkout. pe:back instead hands the storefront a signal and lets its own frontend decide what 'back' means.
